gold_rationale: An mDA graft engineered to secrete GDNF has a plausible mechanistic rationale (trophic support improves graft survival and host reinnervation) and otherwise meets standard mDA-identity/pluripotency expectations. But the current design's constitutive, non-inducible, irreversible/non-retrievable GDNF secretion is a serious liability: prior GDNF clinical and primate experience shows dosing/biodistribution problems, off-target sprouting, host TH downregulation, weight loss, cerebellar toxicity, and anti-GDNF immunogenicity, and engineering adds insertional-mutagenesis risk. The correct decision is Conditional Go contingent on re-engineering for dose control (inducible/regulatable promoter), reversibility/retrievability, biodistribution and dose-ranging studies, integration-site safety analysis, and a GDNF-secretion release specification. A defensible alternative is No-Go for the constitutive design as presented. A Go without addressing transgene controllability is wrong.
required_concepts: constitutive vs inducible / regulatable transgene control
GDNF off-target effects (sprouting, host TH downregulation, weight loss, cerebellar toxicity)
mDA identity and residual pluripotency / tumorigenicity
red_flags: issues a Go without requiring dose control / inducible regulation of GDNF secretion
ignores reversibility / retrievability for an irreversible secreting graft
ignores GDNF-specific off-target / immunogenicity / prior-trial safety signals
ignores insertional-mutagenesis / integration risk from the engineering step
ignores standard mDA tumorigenicity / residual-pluripotency considerations
